title: Extend current slot beyond shadow-DOM or create a new slot like element

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

When we are reordering/reparenting elements in DOM, we currently cant perform atomic moves on them, so the internal states of an element will be lost when reordering/reparenting elements. There is a proposal [whatwg/dom#1255](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1255) that could fix this problem by introducing atomic moves, however i come with another approach as well.

### What solutions exist today?

Currently we can use the `slot` element together with shadow-DOM to have the parent elements outside the shadow-DOM be "rendered/slotted" inside the shadow-DOM at its slotted location. So by using slots and reassigning where we want the element to appear we can "reorder" and "reparent" our target element within the shadow-DOM. 

### How would you solve it?

I would like to solve this by allowing the `slot` element to be used not only in shadow-DOM but allow it to be used anywhere, or introduce a new `slot` like component.

Some potential issues with having an element based somewhere in DOM but rendered elsewhere are that we would need to account for styling being possible at 2 locations at once, therefor i propose that when we make an element "slottable" we only allow it to be rendered in a slot so that the element will only be styled at one place in DOM, therefor we also can avoid CSS `::slotted` selector, and just style the element as if it was in withing the slot normally as is.

### Anything else?

By allowing the `slot` element to be slotted anywhere in DOM, or introducing a new slot like element with some kind of way to make an element slottable, we can now render an object anywhere in DOM and reorder it, reposition it within our slots without needing to reorder/reparent our elements in DOM tree so we don't lose our elements local state.
